question.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{2\times 2}\to R$ defined by $L(A)={y}^{T}Ax$ where 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What is ${∇}_{A}L$ at 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The gradient of $L$ with respect to $A$ is a matrix of the same shape as $A$, with $(i,j)$th entry given by

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}},
$$

the partial derivative of $L$ with respect to the $(i,j)$th entry of $A.$

Writing out $L$ in component-wise notation as 

$$
L={\sum }_{i=1}^{2}{\sum }_{j=1}^{2}{a}_{ij}{y}_{i}{x}_{j},
$$

we have

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}={y}_{i}{x}_{j}.
$$

Thus, ${∇}_{A}L=y\cdot {x}^{T}.$

Evaluating at the given values $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
{∇}_{A}L=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$
